Read the explanations and saved results, expand **Show Python code** when you want
the details, then open the original notebooks in VS Code to experiment.

Start with the [workshop roadmap](00_Workshop_Roadmap.ipynb) and
[setup guide](SETUP_GUIDE.md). To run the examples, download or clone the
[complete repository](https://github.com/thiasyoung/2026-avs-ml-vibe-coding-workshop),
not just one notebook: the examples also use local helper scripts and prepared data.

::: {.callout-note title="A reading view, not a live notebook"}
These pages display the outputs last saved in each notebook. Publishing does not
download data, train models, or refresh results. Blank practice cells are intentional;
missing results are not filled in. Run the downloaded notebooks to generate new results.
:::

## Three workshop modules

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
### 01 · Boiling point

Predict boiling point from molecular structure. Compare a Chemprop graph neural
network, frozen MoLFormer embeddings, and a prompt-built workflow.

[Explore the module](01_boiling_point/README.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### 02 · IR functional groups

Explore how signal conversion, cleansing, padding, and resampling affect a fixed
functional-group classifier. Keep the evaluation data unchanged.

[Explore the module](02_ir_functional_groups/README.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### 03 · HTEM process emulator

Predict local thickness and conductivity from recipes and substrate positions.
Experiment with algorithms using the same prepared features and splits.

[Explore the module](03_htem_conductivity/README.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::
:::

## Read, run, and compare

- **Read:** use the sidebar or search to find a notebook; explanations and saved
  figures remain visible while code is folded.
- **Run:** use the notebook's source link or download the full repository, then follow
  the setup guide and choose the workshop environment in VS Code.
- **Compare:** change the intended part of the workflow and evaluate honestly. More
  elaborate data preparation or a larger model is not guaranteed to improve predictions.
- **Save a PDF:** use your browser's Print → Save as PDF. Expand any code you want
  included before printing; the web view remains the interactive version.
